Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwvwv.dilg.com.ph OPINION NO. 64 s. 2021 SEP 26 HON. NIEL JAKE V. CASI Acting Mayor Pigcawayan, Cotabato Dear Hon. Casi: This has reference to your Memorandum dated July 28, 2023 requesting for an Authority to approve contracts, specifically the engaging in and renewal of contract of services (COS). Per your representation, you assumed as Acting Mayor of Pigcawayan considering the health status of Mayor Juanito C. Agustin after he met a vehicular accident last July 18, 2023. Hence, your herein request for an Authority to prevent the disruption of delivery of services to your constituents and to keep the day-to-day operations of your municipality. At the outset, the Department is of the view that an Authority from its Secretary is no longer necessary for you to enter and approve the contract. May we clarify that your assumption as Acting Mayor of Pigcawayan, Cotabato is automatic by virtue of Section 46(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), thus: (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. (Emphasis Supplied) This provision is reinforced in DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2019-21, Operational Guidelines and Rules Implementing Administrative Order No. 15, Series of 2018, specifically, Item IV(A)(3) thereof, viz: 3. When a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the municipal mayor, the municipal vice-mayor or in case of his/her inability, the highest-ranking sangguniang bayan member, shall automatically exercise the powers "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

and perform the duties and functions of the municipal mayor, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. The Department has been consistent in its legal opinions that the Vice-Mayor acting as Acting Mayor can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Mayor, except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Thus, if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds 30 working days, the Acting Mayor may already proceed to exercise such functions so as not to impair the delivery of vital public service. The appointment, suspension and dismissal of employees mentioned herein pertains to plantilla positions. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 50, series of 2019, we opined that Section 46 (a) of the LGC is not applicable in the case of Job order or Contract of Service because it only refers to the hiring of plantilla positions. Hence, Job order or Contract of Service can be hired by the Acting Mayor anytime pursuant to Section 771 of the LGC. However, please be reminded of the general rule that the local chief executive may enter into a contract on behalf of the LGU upon prior authorization of the sanggunian concerned2. This opinion is based on the facts represented and rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the court. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, UTHORITY OF TH ECRETARY: Y. JUAN VICTOR R. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. - The chief executive of every local government unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the sanggunian concerned, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months.xxx 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 07, S. 2014 dated March 4, 2014 Page 2 of 2
